newsitem.title: UK: Lotus says Yahaya's investments unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Lotus says Yahaya's investments unchanged.

text.p: Group Lotus Ltd, the British sportscar group rescued from a cashflow crisis last year by Malaysia's Hicom Holding Bhd, said it saw no threat to the parent company's investment in Lotus after the death in an accident of Hicom's chairman and main visionary.

Tycoon Yahaya Ahmad, who died in a helicopter crash late on Monday, paid 51 million stg to take control of Lotus in a 1996 deal that also gave its carmaking unit Proton (Perusahaan Otomobil Nasional Bhd ) access to the British company's world-class automotive product and design engineering skills.
In a statement Lotus echoed the wider message already made by the DRB and Hicom groups that there would be continuity across investments masterminded by Yahaya.
"With specific regard to Lotus, the expansion, recruitment and investment programmes of both the engineering and manufacturing divisions will continue as planned," it added.
